gen-gf-gugi-gf-gafata: Gafata reads tall and friendly, its lowercase filling the line with wide-eyed e shapes. Gafata and Gugi share that stature, but Gugi's round letters carry walls as heavy as its straight ones.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-liter: Tall letters, zero stroke contrast. Gugi leads with open-cut terminals and curves matching its stems, while Liter follows in a plain sans with great vertical presence and wide-mouthed rounds.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-miriam-libre: Bold, tall, and a bit cheeky. Gugi is best when its open-cut terminals get room to show off, while Miriam Libre does its best work with a wire-weight line and a generous s.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Chunky headline, spacious text beneath. Gugi earns its keep big and short, where its tall lowercase and open-cut terminals can stand out against Mochiy Pop P One's wide-set letters.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-montserrat-underline: Tall and cut open, then wide and steady. Montserrat Underline brings a plain sans with oversized lowercase and round bowls that never swell, which makes Gugi's tall, open-cut forms feel familiar.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Noto Sans Balinese keeps its short ascenders and breathing curves quiet and modern. Make Gugi small, though, and its contrast-free strokes lose their bold edge, while Noto Sans Balinese holds up fine when sized larger.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads open and modern. Gugi is best when its rope-like strokes get a big stage, whereas Noto Sans Bamum shines in small letters with generous counters.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Gugi draws bold, tall letters with a rolling-ball-pen trail and open-cut terminals, while Noto Sans Bassa Vah answers with a dominant midsection. Their shared tall build is what ties them together.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: A high mean line, open curves. Noto Sans Brahmi would read as a plain sans with easy flow across a page, while Gugi's heavy-to-light-free strokes stay up top.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Gugi's strokes run identical in weight, vertical or horizontal, with tall lowercase nearly touching its capitals. Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of its height too, so the two share a tall frame.
